segments.text: Right now, stones from space are hitting your roof. Tons of them, every single day. You have never heard one land... and the reason why is written in a fourteen hundred year old verse.
segments._shot: meteor streaking across a star-dense sky

segments.text: This is the verse... of the protected ceiling.
segments.title: THE CEILING
segments.titleSub: what the Qur'an calls the sky
segments._shot: slow aurora-like glow rippling on dark sky

segments.text: The Qur'an, the book Muslims believe is the speech of Allah, often points up. To desert people sleeping under the open sky, it kept insisting that what hung above them was not emptiness... it was architecture.
segments._shot: vast desert night sky over dunes, camera tilted up

segments.text: And We made the sky a protected ceiling... but they, from its signs, are turning away.
segments._shot: clouds lit from above, cathedral-like light

segments.text: The classical scholars read it plainly. Ibn Kathir wrote that the sky is a roof over the earth... safe and well-guarded, raised high, protected from anything reaching it. A guarded roof... over every head, everywhere, at once.

Today we can describe some of what that guarding looks like. A blanket of air that burns up the daily rain of space rock into harmless streaks of light... fields that turn away the storms of charged particles the sun throws at us. The verse did not teach that science... it named the mercy, and left the signs open for whoever would look.
segments._shot: shooting stars burning out high in the atmosphere

segments.text: The verse ends with the ache... but they turn away from its signs. Tonight the ceiling above you will quietly absorb a thousand small catastrophes. Don't be the one who never once looked up and said... thank You.
segments._shot: still night sky over a sleeping town
